CPU fallbacks and plan breaks: what cuplyr tells you, and how to hear it

Source: R/execute.R
cuplyr-fallback.Rd

cuplyr runs a dplyr verb on the GPU whenever it can. Two things can happen that you may want to know about. Both are silent by default, and both are always signalled as conditions, so a calling handler sees them whatever the options say.

CPU fallbacks

A verb (or part of one) that has no GPU implementation runs in dplyr on the host: cuplyr collects the table, runs the real dplyr verb and uploads the result. This is correct but slow for a big table. The condition has class cuplyr_cpu_fallback and the fields

  • verb: the verb, as you wrote it ("mutate");

  • expr: the expression that forced the fallback ("qnorm(x / 10)"), or NA when the call as a whole goes;

  • reason: why ("`qnorm()` has no GPU implementation.", a rowwise table, a function of yours that shadows a native one, an unsupported type, ...);

  • rows, cols, bytes: what is collected to the host (the table's dimensions and an estimate of its size; a two-table verb adds both tables).

options(cuplyr.fallback = ) decides what happens next: "silent" (the default), "warn" (a warning of class cuplyr_warning_cpu_fallback) or "error" (an error of class cuplyr_error_fallback, for a script that must stay on the GPU). "warning" is accepted as an alias of "warn". The message reads

cuplyr: mutate() fell back to CPU evaluation for: qnorm(x / 10)
i Reason: `qnorm()` has no GPU implementation.
i Collected 1,000 rows x 3 cols (about 24.4 kB) to run on the CPU.

Plan breaks

A lazy table (the default, tbl_gpu(df)) collects its verbs into a plan and runs it when you compute() or collect(). A few steps need the result of the pending plan before it is asked for (a summarise() of an integer sum(i + j) or max(), a verb that leaves no column). cuplyr then computes the plan early. This stays on the GPU and nothing is collected, but the plan is not fused across that step. The condition has class cuplyr_plan_break and the fields verb, expr, reason and steps (the number of pending steps that ran early).

options(cuplyr.plan_break = ) is "silent" (the default) or "warn" (a warning of class cuplyr_warning_plan_break); "warning" is an alias of "warn". A plan break is never an error: nothing left the GPU.

Invalid option values

Any other value of either option (including "error" for cuplyr.plan_break) warns once per session and value, with class cuplyr_warning_invalid_option (fields option and value), and the default ("silent") is used. All cuplyr options are listed on cuplyr-options.

See also

cuplyr-options for every cuplyr option, and fallback-verbs for the verbs that have no GPU implementation.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Count the fallbacks of a pipeline without changing its behaviour
n <- 0L
res <- withCallingHandlers(
  my_pipeline(),
  cuplyr_cpu_fallback = function(cnd) {
    message("fallback in ", cnd$verb, ": ", cnd$reason)
    n <<- n + 1L
  }
)

options(cuplyr.fallback = "warn", cuplyr.plan_break = "warn")
} # }
